'''''Dactylorhiza foliosa''''', the '''Madeira orchid'''<ref>{{cite web | url = https://gd.eppo.int/taxon/DAKFO | title = ''Dactylorhiza foliosa''
| publisher = EPPO Plant Database | accessdate = 5 September 2019}}</ref> or '''leafy orchid''',<ref name = RHSPF/> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Orchidaceae]], [[endemic]] to the [[Portugal|Portuguese]] Island of [[Madeira]] in the eastern Atlantic Ocean.<ref name="robotmaria">[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=55287 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref>  It is a [[tuber]]ous [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] growing to {{convert|60|cm|0|abbr=on}} and producing spikes of intense, magenta-pink flowers in late spring.<ref>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref>

This plant has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]]<ref name= RHSPF>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Dactylorhiza foliosa''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/5286/Dactylorhiza-foliosa/Details | accessdate=15 April 2020}}</ref> (confirmed 2017).<ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 22 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 24 January 2018}}</ref>

==Synonyms==
*''Orchis foliosa'' <small>Sol. ex Lowe (1831), illegitimate homonym, not Sw. 1800 nor Masson ex Ker Gawl. 1819 nor Spreng. 1826 nor Schur 1866</small>
*''Orchis latifolia'' var. ''foliosa'' <small>Rchb.f. (1851)</small> 
*''Dactylorchis orientalis'' subsp. ''foliosa'' <small>(Rchb.f.) Klinge (1898)</small>
*''Orchis orientalis'' subsp. ''foliosa'' <small>(Rchb.f.) Klinge (1898)</small>
*''Dactylorchis foliosa'' <small>(Rchb.f.) Verm. (1947)</small>
*''Orchis maderensis'' <small>Summerh. (1947 publ. 1948)</small>
*''Dactylorhiza incarnata'' subsp. ''foliosa'' <small>(Rchb.f.) H.Sund. (1975)</small><ref name = robotmaria/>
